text: Tiny floating island at night, a white bunny-ish creature with its back to me, trees. Day 1 with a 30 sec timer, 10 coins, Lv1. A yellow box highlights grass on the left and says 'Tap an empty tile'. I'll tap inside the box.
Oh, it became day 2 and sunny; the bunny turned around, cute. A build menu: Farm $10, Mine (Lv3), Lumberyard (Lv2), Research lab (Lv2), Special 0/1. I have exactly 10 coins. Building a farm.
Farm built in ~4s, coins now 0, got 5 XP. Night again already (days are 30 sec). Bottom shows Sow / Water / Harvest, 5 sec each. Hint says tap the farm to sow. Tapping the farm plot.
Seeds planted (little dots in the soil). Day 3. Now 'Tap again to water -- three times in all'. The hint bubble is covering the bunny's face, a little annoying. Tapping farm to water.
First watering done, sprouts showing. Water button says '10s left' - maybe a cooldown before the next watering? Now hint says 'Tap a Momo' - so the bunny is called a Momo. Tapping it.

Tapped Momo: panel says 'Momo - Free time' with an Assign button. Hint: 'Its tiles light up. The pencil edits them'. I don't really see tiles lighting up, just a ring under Momo. Not sure what 'its tiles' means. Tapping the pencil.

Hmm, Momo wanders around and the pencil moved with it, so my taps kept missing; now the panel closed and the tutorial hint is gone. A bit frustrating chasing a moving target. Let me go back to the farm and water it again (it said three times).

Second watering done, plants are leafy now - nice visible growth. Water shows '9s left', so there's a wait between waterings. While waiting, let me try the Momo again and press Assign this time - maybe it can work the farm for me.

Clearer hint now: 'The pencil edits which tiles this Momo looks after: tap or drag over tiles'. So I paint tiles for the Momo to tend. I want it to look after the farm. Tapping Got it, then the pencil.
Got into edit mode: a checkmark and '0 / 4 tiles'. So the Momo can look after up to 4 tiles. The island seems to be 4 tiles total. Tapping the farm tile to add it.

Farm tile highlighted with a '1' and the Momo walked straight over to it. Panel now: 'Working at Farm, Farm skill 0, 0 jobs, Stays here, Route: Nearest first'. That's satisfying - I've got a worker. Confirming with the checkmark.
Confirmed. Momo is sitting in the farm with a progress ring - it seems to be doing the watering itself. While it works, I'm curious about the Mailbox button top right.
Mailbox: 'No letters yet'. But look - red tomatoes in the farm now! Momo has 1 job done and a '...' speech bubble. Closing mail, peeking at Research.

Research is a big tech tree: tabs Farm, Lumber, Mine, Smelting, Power, Games, Ca(?). First node 'Field expansion' costs 3 flasks + $20, 1 min. I have no flasks and no money, and don't know where flasks come from - probably that Research lab at Lv2. Lots ahead! Closing it, going to watch the harvest.

Momo harvested - farm is empty again, 2 jobs, XP jumped to 29/100. But coins still 0, and there's some cut-off text '1 c...' at the right screen edge under the XP bar that I can't read. Where did the tomatoes go? Do I need to sell them? Checking Status.

Coins went 0 -> 5, so the harvest did sell (just with a delay). Status screen: the island is 'Momonium - A small island, a big tomorrow'. Village -> City goal: Land 4/9, Momo 1/3, Research levels 0/3, Value produced $5/$1.5K. Now I have a long-term goal! Skill bars for Farm/Mine/Lumber/Research/Smelting. Tapping Got it, then Store tab.
Store tab: Crops 0/20, Made 1 - a storage, and the one crop got sold automatically I guess. Momo is on its 4th job, working steadily on its own. Closing this and checking the Shop button bottom left.

Shop has one thing: Hire Momo $25. I only have $5. Each harvest seems to give ~$5, so that's a while. Better plan: when I hit $10, build a second farm on another empty tile. Closing shop and tapping an empty tile to see the build menu.
Build menu again (Farm $10 in red, can't afford). Ooh - Momo has an envelope speech bubble and the Mailbox has a red dot. A letter from the Momo! First, peeking at 'Special 0/1' in the build menu.
Special = landmarks: Clock Tower (Lv5), School (Lv4), Momo Monument (Lv6). One of each, 0/1 slots. Nice long-term carrots. Got it, then reading the letter.
A letter from Momo: 'What if we widened the field?' - cute, the worker is suggesting the Field expansion research. Opening it.

Lovely letter, styled like a real airmail envelope with a flower stamp. Momo proposes Field expansion. 'Let's research it' button. I doubt I can afford it ($20 + 3 flasks), but let's press it and see.

Button now says 'On the research list'. OK. Coins have been stuck at $5 for a few days though, while tomatoes keep growing. Wondering how money comes in. Closing mail and waiting to watch a full cycle.

Another harvest: XP 54/100, but coins STILL $5. That clipped '1 c...' popup appears again at the far right edge - maybe '+1 crop'? It's cut off so I can't read it. Going to the Status > Money tab to understand income.

Money tab: now $10! Income seems to land when the day rolls over ('Yesterday +$5'), with a 7-day bar chart. Also an intriguing 'Island worth $61 - Sell...' button - not touching that! With $10 I'll build a second farm on the empty tile in front.
Second farm going up on the front tile, $0 again. Once it's built I'll add it to Momo's tiles with the pencil so it farms both.
Two farms side by side now, looks great. Sowing the new one myself by tapping it.
Sowing the new farm. Now selecting Momo to add the new farm tile to its route.
Momo is selected, Farm skill went up to 1 after 11 jobs - it's learning! Pencil, then tap the new farm.
2/4 tiles, numbered 1 and 2 - the numbers look like a route order. Confirming. Then I'll try 'Route: Nearest first' to see what it does.

Route switched to 'Row by row' and the tile numbers swapped (front farm is now 1). It says 'Comparing: a few days are needed on each side' - neat, it'll tell me which route is better. Another letter arrived (red dot + envelope over Momo). XP 83/100, close to level 2. Reading the mail.

Second letter: 'Maybe we could water less often' - straw mulch idea, proposes Watering efficiency. Charming that the ideas come from the worker. Accepting it. (Also noticed the 1/2 tile numbers flipped back again - a little confusing which is which.)

Research panel now answers my flask question: the button says 'Build a research lab'. That opens at Lv2 and I'm at 86/100 XP. Hmm, only Field expansion has a yellow dot; the Watering efficiency I just accepted still looks locked. Closing and waiting for level 2.

Panel now reports 'Since the change: 1.4 -> 3 jobs a day' - satisfying, the route change (or the second farm?) doubled output. Not sure which one deserves credit. Still $5 though, money feels slow. XP 88/100. Waiting for level 2.
Both farms are loaded with ripe tomatoes, Momo is harvesting one. Coins have sat at $5 for 3+ days though, which confuses me. I'll help by harvesting the front farm myself.
Level 2! (10/180) - it just quietly ticked over, I almost missed it; no celebration. Research lab and Lumberyard should be open now. Tapping the empty right-hand tile to see their prices.

Unlocked prices: Research lab $45, Lumberyard $80. I have $5 - a long way off at this pace. The clipped '2 c...' popup at the right edge again. Checking the Store tab to see if crops are piling up unsold.
Coins jumped to $15 at the new day - two crops yesterday, $5 each, paid at dawn. Made 5 crops total. Now it clicks: crops sell overnight. Quick peek at the 'Life' tab before time runs out.

Life tab: Happiness 0/100 ('No parks, pubs or halls yet'), Homes 0/0, '1 sleeps outdoors' in red - aww, my poor Momo has no house! But I never saw a house in the build menu. Momo work time x1. That makes me want to give it a home. Saving up $45 for the research lab next.

Stats tab is a wall of numbers: +$2.1/-$1.4 per day, crops 0.4 made/used/sold per day, farm busy 55%/32%, Momo busy 83%, Power 0 kW. Too spreadsheet-y for me right now, but nice for later. Main takeaway: income is ~$2/day and the lab is $45 - slow. Next step would be hiring a second Momo ($25) to work the second farm.
